clue.text: Name that one might drop?

parts.note: surface reading: a person's name, as in name-dropping to impress
setter's reading: a performer's microphone, let fall at the end of a set, is also a man's first name

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the twist: 'name-dropping' is the obvious idiom, but the thing dropped here is a microphone, whose short form doubles as a boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike is both a familiar form of Michael and the informal word for a microphone, famously dropped after a triumphant performance.

clue.text: Female or male? The first one

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for male
in Genesis, the first man created

explanation.surface: A question about sex, as if asking which of the two came first.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to pose a choice between female and male, but 'Female' is the definition and the rest builds the word; it recalls the palindrome 'Madam, I'm Adam'.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a polite form of address for a woman, so it can stand for a female person.

clue.text: Worn-out, bent journalist drinks last half of beer

indicators.note: whoever drinks takes something inside, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: a bent is a natural talent or aptitude

indicators.note: taking the closing half of a word keeps only its final letters

parts.note: the second half of this four-letter word
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A tired, corrupt reporter downs the dregs of a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' reads as crooked, describing the journalist, but it is a noun meaning flair; the whole 'bent journalist' takes ER inside it, between its two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Knackered is informal British slang for exhausted, utterly tired out, so it matches worn-out.

clue.text: Inbred Italian with stunted body parts

indicators.note: something stunted has been kept short, so a letter is cut from the end

parts.note: con is the Italian word for with
the private parts lose their final S

explanation.surface: A cruel picture of an inbred Italian with underdeveloped anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian' looks like a person, but 'Italian with' means the Italian word for with, a translation device.
explanation.definitionFit: Inbred here means innate or present from birth, which is exactly what a congenital condition is.

clue.text: Lots of deliveries made by ramblers starting late

indicators.note: beginning late means missing the opening, so the first letter goes

parts.note: ROVERS, wanderers, without the initial R

explanation.surface: Walkers who set off late place lots of orders for deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests parcels, but it is cricket: a bowler's deliveries are grouped into overs of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, so several overs are many bowled balls.

clue.text: Soldier scattered rubbish after scrubbing uniform filled with earth and garbage

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: to be filled with something is to hold it inside
letters that are scattered are thrown about into a fresh order
scrubbing something out erases it, so a letter is struck from the word

parts.note: the word without U
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
E is the abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: A soldier on cleaning duty strews litter around while his uniform gets dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' is not clothing but the letter U, removed from the rubbish before its letters are shuffled and E is slipped in.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage in its figurative sense is nonsense talk, which is a straightforward synonym of meaningless babble.

clue.text: City and Newcastle's front three turning Roy Keane's head

indicators.note: the front three letters are the first three of the word

parts.note: a first-letters selection: the opening three letters of the city's name

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the initial letter

explanation.walkthrough: The football names are all raw material: Newcastle supplies its first three letters, Roy is reversed and Keane gives only his initial.
explanation.definitionFit: New York is the most populous city in the United States, so it is a simple example of a city.

clue.text: The articles? Tragedian's cap and stockings

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.definitionFit: Pointing at particular items, you would say 'those' to mean the specific things referred to, a demonstrative rather than a grammar term.

clue.text: Last bits of balm (clove oil) tipped on ex- PM's waxy skin

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a link meaning applied to, but it is kept as written; the ex-PM is Robert Peel, founder of the modern police.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon rind is often coated in wax to keep it fresh, so it is a fruit's waxed outer covering.

clue.text: Organisation satisfied with building equipment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Organisation' looks like a firm, but it means orderliness; the hod is the open box on a pole that bricklayers carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Method means orderly arrangement or system in doing things, the abstract sense of good planning and tidiness.

clue.text: Rapper the face of December's Playboy

explanation.definitionFit: Drake is the stage name of the Canadian hip-hop artist, so he is an example of a rapper.

clue.text: Make enough space by moving 14 Across below, having removed bed

once letters have been removed they are taken away from the word

parts.note: the answer to that clue, written out in full
three letters to strike out, one each of B, E and D
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 14 Across is BOREDOM; remove B, E and D and shuffle what remains with BELOW. 'Bed' is not furniture but three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is the idiom for adequate space to move or act freely, sufficient room.

clue.text: Quickly cook hake with steam

definitions.note: an adverb for a verb phrase: 'make haste' means act quickly

indicators.note: to cook can mean to tamper with or doctor, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' sits in a kitchen surface but works as the signal to rearrange the fish and the steam.
explanation.definitionFit: To make haste is to hurry, so the phrase describes doing something rapidly, with speed.

clue.text: Loads of water from broken canoe

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart and its pieces lie in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A damaged canoe takes on lots of water.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'broken' describe a leaking boat, but it signals that the canoe's letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is a vast body of salt water, so it is a huge quantity of the stuff.

clue.text: Tedium arising when old wine is drunk by retired group

indicators.note: what is drunk goes inside the drinker
to retire is to withdraw, going back the way one came

parts.note: a mob is a crowd or gang
O is the abbreviation for old
red wine

explanation.surface: Pensioners at a club grow weary while drinking vintage wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired group' reads like elderly people, but it is a gang turned backwards, which takes the old red wine after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium is the state of being weary and uninterested, which is a direct synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Conduct the opening of Handel's Messiah without soprano after Beethoven's 1st and 8th

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is left out
first and eighth name the positions of the letters to keep

parts.note: the first letter of the composer's name

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the eighth letter of the composer's name
its first letter
SAVIOUR, another name for the Messiah, minus its S
S is the abbreviation for soprano in music

explanation.surface: Instructions to a conductor: perform Handel's Messiah opening without a soprano, after two Beethoven symphonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conduct' tempts as the orchestral verb but is the noun meaning how one behaves; Messiah becomes its synonym before losing the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Conduct as a noun is the way a person acts, which is what behaviour means.

clue.text: Odd animal — male duck? No, shaved emu — in tree

indicators.note: something in another sits inside it

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: shaving trims off the outside, leaving only the central part

parts.note: the middle letter once both ends are removed

explanation.surface: Puzzling over a strange creature: is it a drake? No, a plucked emu sitting in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male duck' suggests a drake, but each word gives letters separately. The answer is the egg-laying mammal group of platypus and echidnas.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotremes, the platypus and echidnas, are mammals that lay eggs, so they are famously peculiar creatures.

clue.text: Irritating leader leaves Scottish church with a few following

indicators.note: when the leader departs, the front letter is gone

parts.note: KIRK is the Scots word for church; its first letter is dropped
some means a few

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like a church head, but it is the first letter of the word for church.
explanation.definitionFit: Irksome describes something tiresome and annoying, a direct synonym of irritating.

clue.text: The result of absent coil?

parts.note: someone off work is away, not present
a coiled length of metal wire that bounces back

explanation.surface: What comes of not having a contraceptive coil fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The coil looks like the contraceptive device, and the result of its absence is a baby; the wordplay just takes the two words literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are children, and a child is literally the product or outcome of a conception.

clue.text: Managing Director of Walls ate raspberry ice-cream after nachos for starters

parts.note: to have a meal is to eat it

indicators.note: starters are the openings, so each word gives its first letter

parts.note: the initial letters of the four words

explanation.walkthrough: Wall's is a British ice-cream maker, so the surface reads as a food executive; really the 'Walls' are Roman fortifications.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor Hadrian ordered the great frontier wall across northern Britain, so he directed its building.

clue.text: Sell sailor's cap in bad condition

parts.note: taken as written

parts.note: its first letter
taken as written

clue.text: Promising Spring, at first — England's freezing by the middle of July

clue.text: Home housing the highest class?

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, since royalty, the top class, live in one; read again, it is the wordplay, a word for home wrapped round the top grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is the official residence of a monarch, who sits at the very top of the social order.

clue.text: Watch one of the Thunderbirds run away
